observations.contents: E7D5 (Slack): Slack logo, question 'このメッセージを送りますか?', warning icon 'external going out', channel metadata (#sales), sender (you), full message preview, timestamp. Buttons: Cancel, Edit, Send (orange). — 91C2 (Gmail): Gmail icon, close button (X), question 'Send this message?', To field (hello@voiceos.com), Subject line (Meeting tomorrow), truncated message preview. Buttons: Send (blue), Edit.
observations.sizes: E7D5 occupies moderate screen space with visible metadata rows; 91C2 is more compact. Both are modal dialogs of similar width; E7D5 slightly taller due to information density.

why.action_clarity: Both ask the same clear, direct question in their respective languages with no ambiguity.
why.parameter_hierarchy: E7D5 layers metadata (warning, channel, sender, message) with clear visual breaks and icon guidance; 91C2 shows only To and Subject.
why.preview_readability: E7D5 displays the full message text untruncated; 91C2 truncates with ellipsis, forcing the user to mentally complete the message.
why.control_visibility: E7D5 presents Cancel as an explicit button alongside Edit and Send; 91C2 hides cancel behind the header X, making the destructive path (sending) more salient.
why.screen_occupation: 91C2 achieves the same confirmation task in a smaller footprint, respecting screen real estate; E7D5 requires more vertical space.
why.visual_craft: 91C2 exhibits refined spacing, optical balance in button sizing, and modern type hierarchy; E7D5 is well-organized but less refined in visual polish.
why.error_prevention: E7D5 flags 'external going out' prominently at the top, explicitly warning of boundary crossing; provides full message preview to verify content. 91C2 relies on To/Subject recognition alone.
why.provenance_visibility: E7D5 shows channel, sender, and timestamp; 91C2 shows recipient and subject only. E7D5 provides fuller context for understanding message origin and destination.
